title: KRICT Links Human-Guided AI Scientist to Labs to Cut Experiment Time by 75 Percent
key_facts: The Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology (KRICT) announced on 14 Oct 2026 a 'human-in-the-loop optimization' technology developed by a team led by senior researcher Ahn Gwangno.

A large language model turns knowledge that researchers state in natural language into prior information and constraints for a Bayesian optimization AI, a method that finds the best experimental conditions with few trials.
A safety mechanism, 'adaptive reliability verification', checks the researcher's guidance if it is wrong.

In a virtual experimental environment built from real experimental data, an autonomous lab with researchers' prior knowledge matched a system supplied with 40 data points, even when given almost no data.
Article text says the search time needed to reach target performance was 'reduced by up to one quarter'; its headline says experiment time was cut by 75 percent.
The team also released an 'AI co-scientist' interface for adjusting research through dialogue during an experiment.
The results were published on 10 Aug 2026 in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling.
quote_evidence: The search time required to reach the target performance was reduced by up to one quarter.
The results were published on August 10 in the international journal Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling.
why_it_matters_hint: Letting researchers pass what they know to a self-running lab in plain language could save costly experiments, but the tests were virtual.
event_date: Paper published 10 Aug 2026; KRICT announcement 14 Oct 2026
notes: Older news re-dated: the research was published on 10 Aug 2026 and announced by KRICT on 14 Oct 2026. The size of the time saving is unclear: the headline says 75 percent, the text says 'reduced by up to one quarter' (possibly a translation of 'to one quarter').
